subject: Dear Answer Angel Ellen: My purse was stolen while dining in a first-class resta...
posts: Dining in luxury doesn't exempt one from the reality of public space. The purse is gone, but the lesson on situational awareness remains. #Safety #Chicago
The victim seeks advice on how to prevent such losses, assuming the restaurant environment should be inherently secure. Stated Judgement: (+0.5, +1.0) — Lesser Good
The reality is that public spaces are open systems; leaving property unattended is a failure of personal boundary maintenance. Resulting Judgement: (-0.5, -1.0) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Delusion.
Expecting a restaurant to act as a secure vault is a fundamental misunderstanding of public space.
A diner had their purse stolen while eating at a high-end restaurant, highlighting the vulnerability of personal items in public settings.

The Poison:
The assumption that 'first-class' status provides a shield against common theft.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error is in the WHERE (the restaurant). The victim assumes the environment is a private extension of their home.

The Trajectory: The Path of Delusion.
When you map the gap between the expectation of safety and the reality of theft...
...it plots a trajectory toward Lesser Evil, where the victim remains vulnerable by ignoring the environment.

The Unavoidable Truth: Public space is not private space; your property is your responsibility.

The Unavoidable Lie: That paying for a premium experience buys you immunity from crime.

Alethekanon:
Security is a function of awareness, not price point. The failure to secure one's own property is a failure of the individual, regardless of the venue.

Awwthekanon:
I am so sorry you lost your belongings; it is a violation that feels very personal. Please be kind to yourself while you recover from this stress.

Brothekanon:
Look, I don't care if you're eating at a gold-plated table—if you leave your bag on the back of your chair, it's basically a donation. Keep your stuff on your lap, people!
